steps.title: Prepare LIT culture medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2 g NaCl, 0.2 g KCl, 4 g Na₂HPO₄, 2.5 g tryptose, and 2.5 g liver infusion broth in 800 mL ultrapure water, ensure complete dissolution, add hemin (10 mg mL⁻¹) after dissolution, adjust pH to 7.2, bring volume to 1 L, dispense into 500 mL glass flasks and autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min; store at 4 °C up to 3 months. Before use supplement with 0.2 % (v/v) 20 % glucose stock (0.2 % final), 10 mL 0.2 % heat‑inactivated FBS, 1 mL 59 mg mL⁻¹ penicillin, and 1 mL 133 mg mL⁻¹ streptomycin; store supplemented medium at 4 °C ≤1 month and warm to 28 °C before use.

steps.title: Prepare TAU artificial urine medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.294 g CaCl₂, 0.406 g MgCl₂, 0.350 g NaHCO₃, 11.1 g NaCl, and 1.267 g KCl in 800 mL ultrapure water, adjust pH to 6.2 with 1 M Na₂HPO₄ stock, bring volume to 1 L, dispense into 500 mL glass flasks and sterilize by 0.22 µm filtration; store at 4 °C up to 3 months and warm to 28 °C before use.

steps.title: Make glucose oxidase (GOX) stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2.42 g PIPES, 38 mg EGTA, and 9 mg MgCl₂ in ultrapure water to 100 mL (final 80 mM PIPES, 1 mM EGTA, 1 mM MgCl₂), adjust pH to 6.9 with NaOH, then add glucose oxidase to give 60 U in 10 mL (6 U mL⁻¹). Aliquot 500 µL, store at –80 °C. For experiments dilute 1:10 in culture medium to 0.6 U mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Prepare PBS buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 8 g NaCl, 0.2 g KCl, 1.15 g Na₂HPO₄, and 0.2 g KH₂PO₄ in 1 L ultrapure water, autoclave at 121 °C, filter through 0.22 µm filter, aliquot into 100 mL flasks, store at room temperature ≤1 month.

steps.title: Prepare hemin stock solution
steps.instruction: Make a paste of 200 mg hemin with 0.2 mL triethanolamine, dissolve in 20 mL ultrapure water to obtain 10 mg mL⁻¹; store at 4 °C up to 6 months.

steps.title: Prepare methoximation solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.045 g O‑methoxyamine hydrochloride in 3 mL pyridine to 15 mg mL⁻¹; store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare internal standard solution
steps.instruction: Dilute pentadecanoic acid in heptane (1 g L⁻¹, 1000 ppm) to 10 ppm by mixing 100 µL stock with 9.9 mL heptane; store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Maintain T. cruzi epimastigotes
steps.instruction: Culture epimastigotes in LIT medium in 75 cm² tissue‑culture flasks at 28 °C (flasks 25–150 cm², upright, non‑adherent).

steps.title: Induce nutritional stress
steps.instruction: When parasites are in exponential phase (~2 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹), collect required volume, centrifuge 2 000 × g 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in PBS to 1 mL. Split evenly, centrifuge again, then resuspend one tube in TAU medium and the other in standard LIT medium to 1 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹. Dispense 20 mL into each of 7 flasks and incubate 3 h at 28 °C.

steps.title: Induce oxidative stress
steps.instruction: Resuspend parasites in LIT medium to 1 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹, dispense 20 mL into each of 14 flasks, incubate 2.5 h at 28 °C. Add 2 mL GOX solution (0.6 U mL⁻¹) to 7 flasks; add GOX buffer (no enzyme) to the remaining 7 flasks. Continue incubation 30 min at 28 °C.

steps.title: Collect parasites after stress
steps.instruction: Pool the total volume from each flask (≈2 × 10⁸ parasites total), transfer to 50 mL centrifuge tubes, centrifuge 2 000 × g 5 min.

steps.title: Wash and deproteinize parasites
steps.instruction: Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL cold PBS, transfer to a microtube, centrifuge 2 000 × g 5 min, discard supernatant, then resuspend pellet in 500 µL cold HPLC‑grade methanol (≥99.8 %).

steps.title: Extract metabolites from culture medium (blank control)
steps.instruction: Place two microtubes containing 300 µL growth medium, add 200 µL cold methanol, vortex 1 min, then centrifuge 17 000 × g 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Centrifuge extracts and store supernatants
steps.instruction: After vortexing the parasite methanol extracts (step above) and the medium controls, centrifuge as described; if analysis is not same‑day, keep the 500 µL supernatant in cryotubes in liquid nitrogen for ≤1 week, then proceed to step B7.

steps.title: Transfer supernatants to GC‑MS vials
steps.instruction: Aliquot 200 µL of each parasite supernatant into GC‑MS vials with glass inserts (no refrigeration needed). Aliquot 200 µL of each blank (medium + methanol) similarly. Combine 28 µL from each of the 7 parasite extracts to make a pooled QC sample and place in a GC‑MS vial. Also place 200 µL cold methanol alone in a vial as methanol control.

steps.title: Dry samples in SpeedVac
steps.instruction: Dry all vials (samples, blanks, QC, methanol control) in a SpeedVac at 30 °C. If not analyzed immediately, store dried pellets at –80 °C in sealed boxes with silica gel inside a plastic bag.

steps.title: Methoximation of dried extracts
steps.instruction: Add 15 µL of the 15 mg mL⁻¹ O‑methoxyamine hydrochloride in pyridine solution to each dried sample, vortex 1 min, ultrasonicate in a bath 40 s, vortex 2 min; repeat vortex‑ultrasound‑vortex cycle three times. Incubate in the dark at room temperature for 16–17 h.

steps.title: Silylation with BSTFA+TMCS
steps.instruction: Add 15 µL BSTFA containing 1 % TMCS to each tube, vortex 5 min, incubate 1 h at 70 °C, then cool 30 min at room temperature in the dark.

steps.title: Add internal standard after derivatization
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of the 10 ppm pentadecanoic acid in heptane internal‑standard solution to each sample, vortex 2 min at room temperature.

steps.title: GC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Inject 1 µL of each prepared sample into an SLB‑5MS fused‑silica column (30 m × 0.25 mm, 0.25 µm film) using an autosampler. Set carrier gas helium flow to 20 mL min⁻¹ (column flow 1.36 mL min⁻¹). Temperature program: start 80 °C, ramp 15 °C min⁻¹ to 300 °C, hold 8 min. Injector 280 °C, transfer line 200 °C, ion source 150 °C, quadrupole 150 °C. Operate in full‑scan mode m/z 40–650 at 70 eV, acquiring 3 spectra s⁻¹. Inject a pooled QC after every four biological samples; inject blank (extraction solvent only) at the beginning, middle, and end of the run. Typical run time ≈34 min.

steps.title: Data acquisition sequence
steps.instruction: Follow the injection order: 1 blank, 2 QC, 3‑6 biological samples, 7 QC, 8‑10 biological samples, 11 blank, 12 QC, then repeat pattern for the full batch.

steps.title: Chromatogram integration in LabSolutions
steps.instruction: Open LabSolutions post‑run analysis, use a QC chromatogram to set integration parameters (slope, width, smoothing) and save as “QC treated”. Apply the same parameters to all chromatograms, generate a compound table with automatic identification using Shimadzu libraries, then manually review and correct peaks using the LabSolutions Browser. For low‑scoring identifications (<80 %) consult external databases (e.g., HMDB) by copying m/z fragments. Save each step.

steps.title: Excel data preprocessing
steps.instruction: Copy the compound tables (names, retention times, areas) into a spreadsheet named “raw data” including samples, blanks, and QCs. Flag missing values (NA) and exclude those metabolites. Create sheet “Organized Data 1” and color‑code zero values red. Move red‑flagged rows to sheet “Removed zero data”. Copy remaining rows to sheet “Organized data IS”. Normalize each metabolite area by the internal‑standard area (Area / Area_IS) and place results in sheet “Organized data after IS”. Remove the IS row, copy normalized data to a new sheet “Organized data after BLK”. Compute the average area of each blank (BLK) and subtract this average from all sample values; discard any resulting negative values (move to “Removed Data”) and rename the sheet “Organized data after BLK”. Copy this to sheet “Organized Data 2”. Identify metabolites using the NIST library; move those with similarity <80 % to sheet “Unidentified data”. For identified metabolites, retrieve common names from HMDB, PubChem, or ChemSpider and place in sheet “Organized Data ID”. Metabolites without any ID go to sheet “Unknown Data”. In sheet “Organized Data ID OK”, sum duplicate metabolites that appear at different retention times (e.g., =SUM(D3:D4)). Remove duplicates, keeping summed values in sheet “Duplicate Data OK”. Calculate relative standard deviation of QC replicates; if CV > 30 % remove that metabolite and place remaining data in sheet “Organized Data QC”. Finally copy the cleaned dataset to sheet “Final Organized Data”.

steps.title: Statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Upload “Final Organized Data” to MetaboAnalyst 6.0. Apply logarithmic transformation for normalization. Perform univariate tests: Student’s t‑test (two groups), ANOVA (multiple groups), Kruskal‑Wallis (non‑parametric). Conduct multivariate analyses (PCA, PLS/OPLS) to detect trends and outliers; exclude outliers only after visual inspection and justification. Use seven biological replicates per condition. Generate Venn diagrams of shared/unique metabolites with Orange 3 or equivalent software.

description: Validation of protocol The method's reproducibility and robustness were validated by the variability observed in seven experimental replicates via principal component analysis (PCA). The treatment types, specifically normal growing vs. nutritionally stressed parasites, significantly cluster apart and from the quality controls ( Figure 5A ). The normalized intensity values were mostly consistent across each metabolite ( Figure 5B ), enabling the identification of the primary metabolic pathways activated by nutritional withdrawal ( Figure 5C ). For additional information, see Silva et al. [5]. Figure 5. Comparative analysis of metabolites in normal growth vs. parasites incubated for 3 h in low-nutrient media (TAU). (A) PCA analysis of each sample and quality control samples. (B) Clustered heatmap of normal growing vs. stressed parasites showing the relative normalized intensities (value). (C) Analysis performed reflecting the enrichment ratio using the T. cruzi KEGG database in the MetaboAnalyst (adapted from Silva et al. [5]).
